stated: Reform UK will detain and deport illegal migrants, including picking them up in small boats and returning them to France, leaving the ECHR, prohibiting resettlement, and barring asylum or citizenship claims for those entering from safe countries. A new Department of Immigration will be created with no legal aid for non-citizens.

source.quote: Stop the Boats with our 4 Point Plan Leave the European Convention on Human Rights. Zero illegal immigrants to be resettled in the UK. New Department of Immigration. Pick up illegal migrants out of boats and take them back to France. Secure Detention for all Illegal Migrants All asylum seekers that arrive illegally from safe countries will be processed rapidly, offshore if necessary. Those entering from a safe country will also be barred from claiming asylum or citizenship. No legal aid for non-citizens. Those rejected will be returned.

bearing_set.reason: The policy is directly about border enforcement, detention, deportation operations and immigration control — a safety/security measure bearing on the justice system, law-enforcement capacity, and national security posture.

Explicitly leaving the ECHR directly alters the UK's legal-rights framework (an O9 indicator by name); removing legal aid for non-citizens raises due-process concerns; barring asylum claims from safe-country entrants affects equal-treatment and rule-of-law protections.

Mass detention powers, picking up people in international waters, and removing legal aid constitute a significant expansion of coercive state power against individuals — the liberty-and-coercion indicators O10 measures, separately from the safety effect scored on O5.

Large-scale detention infrastructure, deportation flights, and a new government department represent concrete public expenditure; UK experience (e.g., Rwanda scheme costs) shows deportation-at-scale is materially expensive, affecting the funded-vs-borrowed balance indicator of O12, even if proponents claim offsetting savings on asylum accommodation.

membership_note: Four fundamentals carry real, non-negligible verdicts: O5 (the policy's stated safety aim), O9 (due process and rule of law via ECHR exit and legal aid removal), O10 (coercive detention and border-enforcement powers as a distinct liberty harm), and O12 (concrete fiscal cost of a new department plus mass deportation operations). Effects on O13, O14, O15 are too indirect or contested to pin to specific indicators at this stage.
